2. Petitioners case is as Follows:
Minor Petitioner no.2 is the daughter of Late Sunil Kumar and Late Smt.Grace Prasanna.
That on 28.05.2024 at 1.25pm, Smt. Grace Prasanna was moving as pillion rider along with her daughter in vehicle bearing Reg No.KA--05-HF-5718 which was driven by her husband Sunil Kumar when they came near Jyotsna Hospital T C Palya road,
Akshaya Nagar, K R Puram, Bengaluru, wherein the Sunil Kumar applied the brake suddenly as a result, Smt.Grace Prasanna fell down to the road, wherein the driver of Car beg. Reg. No.KA-05-ND-9075 drove it with high speed and rash and negligent manner and it ran over Smt.Grace Prasanna,

Akshaya Nagar, K R Puram

sentences.text: In the accident she died due to the grievous injuries.
Autopsy was conducted at East Point hospital.
The guardian of the petitioner has performed funeral and obsequies as per their customs and they have spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- for the same.

3. Guardian of the Petitioner alleged that deceased was 38 yeas of age as on the date of accident and prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy and she was conducting the tution and she was earning Rs.30,000/- per month and she was the only earning member for the family.

He alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and the Jurisdictional police have registered the case against the driver of the aforesaid offending vehicle in Cr.No.130/2024.

Petitioners alleged that the respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and he has insured his vehicle with the respondent No.1, accordingly they are jointly liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and they prays this tribunal to award the compensation amount with interest by allowing the petition.
4. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, Respondent no.2 has not chosen to appear before this tribunal and she placed exparte.
Respondent No.1 appeared through its counsel filed vakalath and written statement by denying the entire version of the petition in toto.
Respondent No.1 has specifically denied the age, income of the deceased.

Respondent No.1 admitted the issuance of policy to the vehicle belongs to respondent No.2 and contended that accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the two wheeler and vehicle belongs to respondent No.2 is falsely implanted in the present case and prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.

5. In order to prove the case, the guardian of the Petitioner No.2 examined himself as PW-2 and examined the IO as PW-3 produced and marked 12 documents which are at Ex.P1 to 12 and they are fully cross examined.
6. Respondent No.1 evidence is taken as nil as prayed for.

sentences.text: According to the guardian of the minor petitioner, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

In order to prove the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, Petitioner has tendered the FIR, complaint, mahazar, sketch,
IMV report, Inquest, PM report, final report, which are at Ex.P1 to 8.
12.

On perusal of the aforesaid documents it is evident that Smt.Grace Prasanna died in the motor vehicle road accident caused by the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle that is Rangaswamy s/o Gurumurthy.K.

Further more, Ex.P.10 is the reply notice wherein respondent No.2 admitted that Rangaswamy was the driver of her vehicle and he was having valid DL and the policy issued for her vehicle was valid as on the date of the accident.
The Mahazar, Sketch, IMV, final report establish the involvement of the offending vehicle and the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
13. Respondents have not disputed the aforesaid documents nor placed the evidence to probabilise their contention as contended in their written statement.
Respondent No.1 has failed to establish their contention that accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the two wheeler that is Late Sunil Kumar S/o D.Dayalan.
PW-2 being the IO of the case, in his cross examination he admitted that there is no negligence on the part of the deceased Sunil Kumar in the alleged accident.
It is true that Sunil Kumar is arrayed as accused No.2 for contravention of section 146, 196,192 of IMV Act.
Respondent No.1 has failed to plead the alleged negligent act of the Sunil kumar nor suggested the same to PW-2.
They failed to establish the fact that triple riding is the main and sole cause for the accident.
Respondents have not challenged the final report which is at Ex.P.8, which was filed after through investigation and it has reached its finality.
Further more the petitioners version and the documents remain un-impeached and unrebutted.

14. Petitioners have not tendered the evidence to substantiate the nature of work and the income of the deceased accordingly the notional income of Rs.16,500/- has to be considered as the income of the deceased as the accident occurred in the year 2024.
15. Further more
as per the entry in Aadhar card of the deceased which is Ex.P.11, the date of birth of the deceased is 26.12.1985.
Accordingly the age of the deceased as on the date of the accident was 38 years, 5 months, 2 days and multiplier 15 is applicable.
16. Deceased was self employee, married and she was below 45 years, accordingly 40% should be added towards her monthly income for future prospectus.
Deceased left behind one dependent accordingly 1/3 should be deducted from his monthly income towards his personal expenses.

17. The loss of dependency is calculated as follows:
1 Monthly income Rs. 16,500/-
Add: 40% of income future prospectus Rs. 6,600/-

Monthly income Rs. 23,100/-
2 Less; 1/3 for personal expenses Rs. 7,700/-

 Rs.15,400 (income)X 12 (month) X 15 Rs.27,72,000/-

sentences.text: Accordingly petitioners are entitled for Rs.27,72,000/- as compensation under the head Loss of Dependency.

18. Loss of estate;
As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranaya sethi case, Tribunal has to award Rs.15,000/- as compensation under this head.

19 . Funeral Expenses, transportation etc., Accordingly as per the judgment in Praneya sethi case,
minimum amount of Rs.15,000/- can be awarded under this head.
20. Loss of Consortium :
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma GIC V/s Nanuram case, wherein the concept of consortium is categorically discussed.
In the present case minor petitioner no.2 is the daughter of the deceased and she is entitled for consortium of Rs.40,000/-.
Except the aforesaid compensation amount, petitioners are not entitled for compensation in any other heads.
21. In total the petitioners are entitled for compensation as follows;
Sl Compensation under the Head Amount No. 1 Loss of dependency Rs.27,72,000/-

2 Loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-
3
Funeral expenses & transportation Rs. 15,000/- 4 Loss of Consortium Rs. 40,000/-
[S In total petitioners are entitled for compensation amount of Rs.28,42,000/-.

22 Rate of Interest: The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

sentences.text: Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
23. Liability:
Admittedly the validity of the insurance policy of the offending vehicle is not disputed nor denied by the respondent No.1.

Further more, the driver of the offending vehicle could have been stopped while seeing Smt.Grace Prasanna falling on the road, respondent No.1 has failed to probabilise the fact that accident occurred due to the negligent act of the driver of the two wheeler.

Accordingly respondent no.1 is directed to pay the compensation amount along interest before this tribunal with in one month from the date of the Judgment.

Accordingly I am answering Issue no.1 in the affirmative, Issue no.2, in the negative and issue No.3 in partly affirmative,

For the foregoing reason and discussion, on the aforesaid points, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is partly allowed with cost.
